title: Define interop declaration and acceptance criteria for unpinned community model intake
creator: Aisha Mendez
body:
Summary:
We need a concise, machine- and human-readable 'interop declaration' that every new community/unpinned model entry must supply. The declaration should capture the minimum runtime assumptions and compatibility signals required by the serving runtime and catalog consumers so we can accept more unpinned community variants with predictable behavior and automated fallbacks.

Goals:
- Reduce onboarding time for community models by surfacing critical runtime expectations (tokenization, context window, kv-cache semantics, attention type hints, fp/quantization tolerances).
- Provide an acceptance checklist that gates catalog ingestion for unpinned entries (i.e., variants that are not pinned to a specific runtime-validated binary).
- Enable runtime to make deterministic fallback/routing decisions when an unpinned variant exhibits incompatible behavior.
- Ensure we capture signals that allow automated profiling and a lightweight sanity suite to catch regressions before public listing.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define the interop declaration schema (fields, enums, required/optional markers).
- Define acceptance criteria for 'unlisted/unpinned' community model intake (sanity tests, perf ceilings, and clear rollback triggers).
- Mapping from declaration fields -> runtime guards (simple decision table for routing and fallback).
- Confluence PRD and intake form updates; short guide for Solutions/Support.

Out-of-scope:
- Full runtime implementation of fallback routing (engineering will own execution tickets).
- Deep auto-quantization or kernel tuning (research/infra).

Requirements (high level):
1) Interop Declaration Schema must include the following required fields:
   - tokenizer_hint (enum: bpe, sentencepiece, wordpiece, other)
   - vocab_size_hint (integer or string)
   - max_context_tokens (integer)
   - kv_cache_compatible (enum: full | prefix-only | none)
   - attention_type (enum: dense | sparse | local | rotary | other)
   - numeric_precision (enum: fp32 | fp16 | int8 | int4 | dynamic)
   - recommended_runtime_flags (list of short strings)
   - test_prompt_set_link (string URL to canonical prompt set)
2) Declaration must be both human-readable (one-paragraph summary) and machine-parseable (JSON schema).
3) Acceptance checklist for unpinned entries (all must pass unless a documented exemption exists):
   - Tokenization parity check: 5 curated prompts -> tokenization delta <= 2 tokens per prompt vs declared tokenizer behavior.
   - Context sanity: model must accept and produce a meaningful response for 2x declared max_context tokens (or fail with documented error).
   - KV cache smoke: if kv_cache_compatible != none, a 4-turn chat scenario preserves non-trivial context (simple heuristic match on repeated entity).
   - Latency profile: 95th percentile within catalog baseline for the declared precision and hardware class (or flagged with performance note).
   - Determinism bias: for deterministic-expected variants, repeated calls with fixed seed produce <= 5% token-level divergence.
4) Acceptance metadata stored in catalog entry: declaration_json (raw), intake_verifier (github/pr link), verified_by (user id), verified_at (date string), verification_artifacts (list of urls).

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- PRD and schema reviewed and signed off by Runtime, Research, and Legal.
- Updated intake form implemented in Confluence (link placeholder) and the public intake flow includes the new declaration JSON field.
- Automated sanity-run harness (lightweight) can be executed from a dev VM to validate the five checks above and emits a machine-readable verification artifact.
- For any unpinned entry accepted under this flow, the catalog page must show 'interop-declaration: verified' with a badge and link to verification artifacts.
- If any sanity check fails, the model is flagged as 'requires-pin' and a recommended fallback variant (if available) is attached.

Design/UX notes:
- The public-facing intake should not expose the entire schema to users; use progressive disclosure (human summary + advanced toggle for JSON).
- Operators (Solutions/Support) should have a one-click re-run of the sanity harness and a timeline of verification artifacts.

Rollout plan and milestones:
- Week 1 (now): Finalize schema and acceptance checklist. (PM lead: Aisha; reviewers: Runtime/Research/Legal)
- Week 2: Build Confluence intake form + developer-facing JSON schema. Start engineering ticket for sanity harness (ENG-51234).
- Week 3: Pilot with 3 community model submissions; iterate on thresholds.
- Week 4: Launch catalog UI badge and intake enforcement for new submissions only.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strict should tokenizer parity be? Tight check increases false rejects for creative tokenizers. We propose soft enforcement with a 'tokenization_notes' field and increase manual review when delta > 5 tokens.
- Should we allow a temporary 'experimental' flag for models that pass most checks but fail a non-safety perf target? Proposed: allow 14-day experimental listing with automatic visibility limits and an explicit user warning.
- Verification artifacts introduce storage and retention needs; propose 90-day retention for artifacts tied to unpinned verification.

Telemetry and observability:
- Add an intake funnel metric: submissions -> verified -> listed -> pinned-conversion-rate.
- Track sanity harness false-positive rate and manual review overhead.

Acceptance tests / QA:
- Test plan attached: run harness on internal testbench with three synthetic community variants (links to GH testcases).
- Edge-case test: model that declares kv_cache_compatible=prefix-only but returns inconsistent entities across turns. Expected: harness flags and prevents autopublication.

comments: 2025-03-11 - Priya Patel (Runtime): Reviewed schema draft; asked to add kv_cache_compatible enum and an explicit determinism signal. Noted that attention_type 'rotary' may be insufficiently descriptive for some architectures.

2025-03-12 - Mateo Alvarez (Research): Suggested adding 'test_prompt_set_link' and a small recommended prompt corpus for each model class; proposed a 'sanity score' aggregation to simplify acceptance decisions.
2025-03-13 - Legal (Hannah Cho): Approved the approach for public listings; requested retention policy for verification artifacts and a short privacy blurb for examples retained from model vendors.
2025-03-15 - Designer (Keiko Tanaka): UX notes added — progressive disclosure for the JSON declaration in the intake; draft badge visuals attached in Confluence (link placeholder).
2025-03-16 - Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Created ENG-51234 to implement harness; proposed runtime decision table in the ticket and scheduled a sync with infra next Tuesday.
2025-03-18 - Aisha Mendez (PM): Incorporated feedback; marking PRD as 'In Review' and requesting Runtime lead sign-off by 2025-03-21.
